title: This 16-Year-Old Founded an AI Missile Startup. He’s Targeting ‘Cost per Kill’
gist: Latvian-born 16-year-old Henrijs Dandzbergs, likely Y Combinator's youngest solo founder, is building Polemos Industries to make cheap, portable, jam-resistant AI-guided missiles with an explicit goal of lowering 'cost per kill.' The profile shows YC's willingness to back long-shot defense ideas despite heavy competition from Anduril, Leidos and others and the hard engineering trade-offs of cheap precision missiles, along with unresolved ethical questions.

insights.claim: Polemos Industries, founded by 16-year-old Henrijs Dandzbergs, is developing a class of precision-guided missiles meant to be cheap and easy to manufacture, fired from portable launchers and resistant to jamming, with its investor one-pager framing the goal as reducing 'cost per kill.'

insights.so_what: Cost-per-effect is becoming the core metric in defense tech after Ukraine, favoring startups that promise mass-producible precision munitions.
